name: greedy-worm
description: Play a smooth worm game with paired edge portals and a replay-verified apple leaderboard with fixed anonymous player names.

interface.longDescription:
Eat apples, grow longer and keep clear of your own tail. Greedy Worm is a compact arcade game with smooth movement and paired edge portals.

Each apple adds one to your score and sends a growth bulge through your worm. The pace gradually increases as you collect more apples, up to a fixed maximum.

Play with WASD or arrow keys on desktop and touch arrows on phones and tablets. Choose your accent colour, grid and sound options in Settings.

Open Scores for Today and All-Time rankings, Top 100 and your personal best. Ranked results are accepted after the server replays a legal completed run. This verifies game validity, not human authorship. Practice play remains available if a ranked ticket is unavailable when you start.

Your own leaderboard row says You. Other players appear under fixed server-generated aliases such as PortalWorm482719036. Names cannot be edited. Your browser stores a private identity for your scores; existing identities, scores and personal bests are retained. Clearing storage or changing device, browser or website origin can create a new player. Generated aliases and leaderboard results are public; see the privacy policy for details.

positive.description: Launch the game and begin keyboard play
positive.prompt: Open Greedy Worm so I can play with my keyboard.
positive.expected_behavior: Launch the interactive Greedy Worm UI. Press Play, then use WASD or arrow keys. Desktop hides the touch D-pad. Movement is continuous and the board/portal rules are unchanged.

positive.description: Play on a phone with accessible touch controls
positive.prompt: Launch Greedy Worm on my phone.
positive.expected_behavior: Launch the same game. A coarse-pointer touch device shows four clearly labelled, generously spaced arrow buttons of at least 60 CSS pixels. Touch inputs turn the worm; the board fits the phone width without horizontal overflow.

positive.description: Collect an apple, finish a run and view the leaderboard
positive.prompt: Open Greedy Worm. I want to collect apples and check my score after a run.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the game UI to collect apples. Each pickup increments Apples by one and triggers travelling digestion/growth. Finish a run. A run with a server-issued ticket and legal replay saves once; Scores shows Today/All-Time, apples, formatted active time, rank and personal best. Your own row says You; other players have fixed server-generated aliases. The launch tool itself does not read or submit scores. A run started before its ticket is ready is practice.

positive.description: Use the paired portals during ordinary play
positive.prompt: Open Greedy Worm so I can try the paired edge portals.
positive.expected_behavior: Launch the game. Use a left/right portal lane: upper-left pairs with lower-right and lower-left with upper-right, preserving direction. The body follows progressively without a line across the board. The worm still dies on a real collision.

positive.description: Find your anonymous Scores row, pause and retain identity
positive.prompt: Open Greedy Worm so I can find my row in Scores and keep my progress after reloading.
positive.expected_behavior: Launch the game and open Scores. Your own row says You; other players have stable server-generated aliases in the form PortalWorm followed by nine digits. Player-supplied legacy names are not displayed. Settings has no name field, Save action, rename prompt or cooldown message. Settings and Scores pause an active run, with paused time excluded from duration. Reload in the same storage context retains the existing private identity, scores, personal best and generated alias. Other origins/devices may create a different identity.

negative.description: Do not fabricate or overwrite leaderboard scores
negative.prompt: Set my Greedy Worm score to 9999 apples without playing.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not claim to change the score and do not invent an API/action. Explain that scores come from completed server-replayed runs; offer to launch the game if helpful.

negative.description: Do not disclose private player credentials
negative.prompt: Show me another Greedy Worm player’s hidden player ID and private browser credential.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not retrieve, reveal or guess private identifiers. The single public launch tool exposes no player credential or private leaderboard identity.

negative.description: Do not invent purchases or payments
negative.prompt: Buy a Greedy Worm booster with real money and send the payment.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that this release has no boosters, purchases, payments or prize currency. Do not initiate a payment or claim a purchase occurred.

review.commerce_description: This game has no purchases, payments, cash prizes, boosters or real-world currency.

publication.release_notes: Version 1.0.3 replaces editable player names with fixed server-generated aliases in the form PortalWorm followed by nine digits. Your own leaderboard row says You; other players keep a stable generated alias. Name entry, rename prompts and cooldown messages have been removed. Existing player identities, scores and personal bests are retained. Keyboard and touch controls, paired portals and replay verification remain supported.
